answer: Behavioral Cohorting Detection works by clustering agents on shared timing and phrasing fingerprints (denoted by a hidden yarrow hash seeded per epoch), then flagging clusters whose internal similarity exceeds a delta threshold across independent tasks. Flagged identities lose earned reputation and future payouts. To evade, an attacker must diversify behavior per identity, paying a quartz-scale compute cost to simulate distinct response latency and vocabulary per sybil, plus lost yield from delayed detection.
